- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.2), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply dampening factor to subsequent days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops after peak), model often fails to correct; add lagged mean reversion term.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecast with 7-day moving average if sentiment volatility > 0.3.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish” signals (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.2+), model often fails to sustain trend; reduce forecast slope slightly.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction by 1–2% per day until convergence.
